```{.r .cell-code}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

cars <- mtcars |>
  tibble::as_tibble(rownames = "model") |>
  mutate(
    cylinders   = factor(cyl, levels = c(4, 6, 8), labels = c("4-cyl", "6-cyl", "8-cyl")),
    transmission = factor(am, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Automatic", "Manual"))
  )

glimpse(cars)
```

## Weight against fuel economy

Heavier cars drink more, and the relationship is close to linear within each
cylinder count.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(cars, aes(wt * 1000, mpg, colour = cylinders)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, alpha = .85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = .7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2f6f4e", "#c08a2e", "#8c3b3b")) +
  labs(
    x = "Weight (lb)", y = "Miles per gallon", colour = NULL,
    title = "Fuel economy against weight",
    subtitle = "32 cars, Motor Trend 1974"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Fuel economy falls with weight; the gap between 4- and 8-cylinder cars persists at any given weight.](index_files/figure-html/fig-weight-mpg-1.png){#fig-weight-mpg width=672}
:::
:::

## A quick model


::: {#tbl-model .cell tbl-cap='Least-squares fit of mpg on weight and cylinder count.'}

```{.r .cell-code}
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cylinders, data = cars)

broom::tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|term           | estimate| std.error| statistic| p.value| conf.low| conf.high|
|:--------------|--------:|---------:|---------:|-------:|--------:|---------:|
|(Intercept)    |    33.99|      1.89|     18.01|       0|    30.12|     37.86|
|wt             |    -3.21|      0.75|     -4.25|       0|    -4.75|     -1.66|
|cylinders6-cyl |    -4.26|      1.39|     -3.07|       0|    -7.09|     -1.42|
|cylinders8-cyl |    -6.07|      1.65|     -3.67|       0|    -9.46|     -2.69|


:::
:::


Each extra 1000 lb costs roughly 3.2 mpg, holding
cylinder count fixed. That number isn't typed in — it's an *inline* R expression,
written like this:

```markdown
Each extra 1000 lb costs roughly 3.2 mpg.
```

(In a `.qmd` the inline form is a backtick span starting with `r`.) Refit the model
and the sentence updates itself, so the prose can never drift away from the numbers.

## Group summaries


::: {#tbl-summary .cell tbl-cap='Mean fuel economy by cylinder count and transmission.'}

```{.r .cell-code}
cars |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_mpg = round(mean(mpg), 1),
    sd_mpg   = round(sd(mpg), 1),
    .by = c(cylinders, transmission)
  ) |>
  arrange(cylinders, transmission) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Cylinders", "Transmission", "n", "Mean mpg", "SD"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
